mappings.rationale: An entity-wide data management and personal data protection strategy with vision, objectives, metrics and budget is exactly the data governance program (GOV-10) plus its strategic plan and objectives (PRM-01.1), with the privacy half covered by the data privacy program (PRI-01).
Adopting the national program's guiding principles to anchor the entity's data agenda is the definition of business context/mission (GOV-08) and the derivation of control objectives from it (GOV-09).
A 3-year prioritized implementation roadmap with initiative sequencing is a strategic plan and objectives artifact (PRM-01.1) coupled with the allocation of resources to those initiatives (PRM-03).
Formal approval by the Data Management Committee is steering-committee program oversight (GOV-01.1); socializing the strategy in internal workshops is the publishing/dissemination step of GOV-02.

Analyzing national, sector-regulator and internal data requirements to find policy gaps is the identification of applicable statutory/regulatory obligations (CPL-01) and the scoping of what those obligations cover (CPL-01.2).

Developing and issuing entity-specific data management and personal data protection policies and guidelines is the documented-policy publication control (GOV-02) applied to the data governance (GOV-10) and privacy (PRI-01) programs.
Mandatory training on national data laws and on every data management domain addressed to the specific data roles is general awareness training (SAT-02) plus role-based training (SAT-03).
Standing up a Data Management Office to own the data agenda is the formal assignment of program responsibilities (GOV-04) instantiated for the data governance function (GOV-10).
A Data Management Committee giving direction and oversight to the data agenda is literally SCF's Data Management Board (PRI-13) and its steering-committee oversight function (GOV-01.1).

Appointing a Chief Data Officer with a documented job description is assigned program responsibility (GOV-04) within a defined stakeholder accountability structure (GOV-04.1); SCF names a CPO/DPO but has no CDO-specific control.
The Data Governance Officer role is an assigned governance responsibility (GOV-04) whose duties are the stewardship of data assets described in DCH-01.1.
The Open Data and Information Access Officer is an assigned role (GOV-04) accountable for the entity's publicly accessible content and information-access requests (DCH-15).
A Compliance Officer appointed to audit and monitor the data agenda is the internal audit function (CPL-02.1) staffed through assigned responsibility (GOV-04).
Appointing a Personal Data Protection Officer with a documented mandate is the Data Protection Officer control (PRI-01.4) verbatim in substance.

Business Data Executives own data for their business domain, which is asset/data ownership assignment (AST-03) exercised through the stewardship structure (DCH-01.1) and formal role assignment (GOV-04).
Business Data Stewards appointed per domain are precisely the data stewardship role defined in DCH-01.1.
IT Data Stewards are the technical counterpart of data stewardship (DCH-01.1) and carry ownership accountability for the underlying data assets (AST-03).
A Legal Advisor appointed to support data-related regulatory matters is the legal capability behind statutory/regulatory compliance (CPL-01), assigned as a defined responsibility (GOV-04).

Defining audit scope, audit planning/execution, findings reporting and non-compliance escalation is controls oversight (CPL-02) delivered through periodic audits (CPL-02.2) and audit activities (CPL-04).

An audit report stating compliance per specification with supporting evidence is the ability to demonstrate conformity (CPL-01.3); the remediation recommendations with owners and target dates are corrective action (CPL-02.3).
Generating and monitoring recurring compliance audit scores against the national framework is control conformity monitoring (CPL-03) trending toward continuous control monitoring (CPL-03.8).
Periodic review of the data management plan with documented outcomes and recorded changes is the periodic review and update of the program (GOV-03).
An ongoing capability to communicate program activities, metrics, policy updates and compliance scores is program status reporting (GOV-17) including reporting to the governing body (GOV-01.2).
A defined set of data governance KPIs (role assignment, meetings held, training completion, audit score, issue cycle time) is measures of performance (GOV-05) expressed as KPIs (GOV-05.1).
Defining, implementing and monitoring continuous improvement mechanisms across all domains is the commitment to continual improvements control (GOV-01.3).
A register of CDO-approved governance decisions with their justifications is the decision-record layer of data governance (GOV-10) and constitutes defensible evidence of due diligence (CPL-13.1).
A historical register of reported data management issues and their resolutions is the deficiency tracking register described in IAO-05, applied to data rather than security findings.
Version control over data management documents is only weakly covered: SCF treats documentation issuance and maintenance under GOV-02 and has no dedicated document-versioning control.
A plan with roadmap, milestones, resources and budget to implement the entity's Data Catalog tool is the Data Catalog control (GOV-10.1) plus the strategic plan artifact that carries it (PRM-01.1).
Prioritizing which data sources enter the catalog and defining their business/technical metadata is scoping the Data Catalog (GOV-10.1) and building the underlying asset inventory (AST-02).
A target metadata architecture (sources, central repository, flows, model) is the architecture of the Data Catalog (GOV-10.1) developed in alignment with enterprise architecture (SEA-02).

Approving which data sources the catalog tool may connect to is an authorized-to-connect decision (AST-01.5), and approving employee access to the tool is the definition of access authorizations over the data it exposes (DCH-01.4, ISO 5.18).

Role-based catalog access groups (read-only, read-update, administrator) scoped by metadata scope is defining access authorizations (DCH-01.4) and enforcing them by role (IAC-20, ISO 5.18 provisioning of access rights).
Tool training targeted only at employees who discover, analyze or administer metadata is role-based training (SAT-03) rather than general awareness.

Naming catalog power users as coaches and running a communication plan to drive adoption is organizational knowledge sharing (SAT-05) layered on the role-based training (SAT-03) this specification repeats.
Assigning Business and IT Data Stewards to every metadata entry, kept current, is data stewardship (DCH-01.1) implemented as per-asset ownership assignment (AST-03).
A workflow-driven process for registering and populating metadata is the operating procedure of the Data Catalog (GOV-10.1) and keeps the data asset inventory populated (AST-02).
A mandated metadata attribute structure that entities may extend is the catalog's data model (GOV-10.1) expressed as required asset attributes (AST-31.3).
A workflow for updating metadata keeps the catalog current, which is the Data Catalog control (GOV-10.1) and the inventory-update-on-change requirement (AST-02.1).
Identifying metadata quality issues, reporting them and remediating within SLAs is data quality operations (DCH-22) under a data quality management regime (PRI-10), applied to metadata.
Reviewing user-added tags and comments on catalog metadata is the governance of data tags (DCH-22.2) and of data protection attributes attached to assets (DCH-05).
Reviewing user-assigned trust certificates is a catalog-internal trust signal (GOV-10.1) closest in intent to asserting data provenance (AST-03.2); SCF has no certification-of-metadata control.

Implementing the catalog tool explicitly as 'an inventory of the Entity's data assets' is the Data Catalog control (GOV-10.1) doubling as the asset inventory (AST-02) and sensitive data inventory (DCH-06.2).
Automated notifications so catalog users learn of metadata changes is stakeholder notification of changes (CHG-05) implemented inside the Data Catalog (GOV-10.1).
Tracking catalog user logins and invoked operations and storing the resulting activity logs as artifacts is event log collection (MON-02) with defined log content (MON-03), i.e. ISO 8.15 logging.

Keeping the catalog tool on the latest vendor release, or documenting an analyzed rationale for not doing so, is software patching (VPM-05) on stable versions (VPM-04.1) and avoiding unsupported technology (TDA-17).
Catalog usage and adoption statistics (registered/active users, logins, queries, annotations, ratings) are program key performance indicators (GOV-05.1).
Completeness, accuracy and consistency KPIs for metadata are performance indicators (GOV-05.1) measuring a data quality management program (PRI-10).
Ranking data by importance so master data is assessed first is scoping the data quality management program (PRI-10) ahead of data quality operations (DCH-22).
A Data Quality Plan with roadmap, milestones, resources and budget is a data quality management program (PRI-10) carried by a strategic plan artifact (PRM-01.1).

Collecting quality requirements, defining rules, profiling data, reporting issues and building remediation plans with root cause and impact analysis is exactly data quality operations (DCH-22) under a data quality management program (PRI-10).

Documenting data quality rules with owners and mapping each to completeness/uniqueness/timeliness/validity/accuracy dimensions is the rule layer of data quality operations (DCH-22) and data quality management (PRI-10).

Scheduled or event-triggered execution of data quality rules with issue reporting to stewards and executives is ongoing data quality operations (DCH-22) delivered through data quality automation (PRI-10.1).

Root cause analysis, option selection, cleansing where the source cannot be fixed, and verification that the issue closed is the corrective action cycle (CPL-02.3) applied to data quality operations (DCH-22).
SLAs with deadlines for remediation planning, implementation and escalation on breach are the performance targets (GOV-05) governing the data quality issue process (DCH-22).
Tooling for data profiling, rule management and issue workflow automation is data quality automation (PRI-10.1) supporting data quality operations (DCH-22).
Trending issue counts and deployed rule counts against targets is KPI measurement (GOV-05.1) of the data quality operations program (DCH-22).
Resolved-vs-reported counts, overdue counts and mean remediation times are process performance indicators (GOV-05.1).
Mandatory data quality reviews inside the SDLC that must be remediated before promotion to production is a testing gate throughout development (TDA-09) enforcing data quality operations (DCH-22).
A user-facing workflow to report data quality issues to stewards is the intake side of data quality operations (DCH-22) feeding a deficiency tracking register (IAO-05).
Publishing data quality rules and monitoring results as metadata in the catalog is populating the Data Catalog (GOV-10.1) with data quality operations output (DCH-22).
A Data Operations Plan orchestrating data operations activities with roadmap and budget is operations management (OPS-01) driven by a strategic plan artifact (PRM-01.1).

Forecasting future storage capacity from historical trends, application performance and the application roadmap, including budget estimation, is capacity planning (CAP-03) within capacity and performance management (CAP-01).
Ranking information systems by business criticality and by monetary/reputational loss to set recovery order is identification of critical assets (BCD-02) driven by business impact analysis (RSK-08).

A documented evaluation process for selecting DBMS software weighing cost, skills, scalability, reliability and the security controls the technology provides is technology acquisition (TDA-01) applied to a COTS product selection (TDA-03).

A storage and retention policy setting retention periods by type/classification/legal requirement plus disposal and destruction rules is media and data retention (DCH-18) and information disposal (DCH-21/ISO 8.10), with the storage-protection clause covered by DCH-06.

Regular reporting of database capacity, availability, query execution times and change tracking is performance monitoring (CAP-04) of the DBMS (AST-28.1), with the change-tracking element resting on database logging (MON-03.7).

Role-based database access where roles are defined by the data classification standard is database administrative access control (AST-28) implementing classification-driven access authorizations (DCH-01.4), i.e. ISO 8.3 information access restriction.

Configuration identification, change control, status accounting and configuration audits against the documented baseline is a configuration management program (CFG-01) with baselines (CFG-02) and configuration change control (CHG-02) - ISO 8.9 verbatim.
Keeping DBMS tools on the latest vendor release or holding a documented rationale for the release strategy is software patching (VPM-05) and management of unsupported technology (TDA-17).

SLAs fixing database availability windows, maximum transaction execution time and escalation on breach are capacity and performance management targets (CAP-01) enforced by performance monitoring (CAP-04).

Defining backup frequency and scope per system, backup medium and physical location, and periodically validating backups on non-production copies is data backup (BCD-11) with restore testing for reliability and integrity (BCD-11.1).

A DR plan with prioritized recovery order, response roles, damage-mitigation actions and per-system RPO/RTO is a BC/DR plan (BCD-01.7) with defined recovery objectives (BCD-01.4) and recovery/reconstitution activities (BCD-12) - ISO 5.30 ICT readiness.

Despite its title, the text requires a change-request-driven process for implementing database changes to production with defined rollback actions, which is configuration change control (CHG-02) with access restriction for change (CHG-04), ISO 8.32.
Storage utilization percentages, transaction counts and average query times are capacity performance monitoring outputs (CAP-04) reported as KPIs (GOV-05.1).
A plan to control the document and content lifecycle with roadmap, resources and budget is data governance applied to documents (GOV-10) via a strategic plan artifact (PRM-01.1).

Migrating paper records to electronic format and eliminating paper creation is a digitization initiative with no security or privacy analogue in SCF; only the generic data governance umbrella (GOV-10) touches it.
Producing a ranked list of documents to load into the DMS is a scoping exercise over the document inventory (AST-02) under data governance (GOV-10); SCF has no prioritization control.
Identifying and ranking key processes to be implemented as DMS workflows is business process definition (PRM-06).

A policy covering naming conventions, assignment of classification levels, access approval, backup/recovery and retention/disposal for documents is data protection policy (DCH-01) with classification (DCH-02) and retention (DCH-18).
Training employees on document and content management policies and on the DMS/CMS tooling is role-based training (SAT-03).
Bringing document and content management systems into the entity's backup and recovery plan is directly the data backup control (BCD-11), ISO 8.13.

Handing documents to the archival facility and physically destroying them including overwriting and secure deletion is retention (DCH-18) followed by information disposal (DCH-21) and physical media disposal (DCH-08), ISO 8.10.

Role-based access to documents where the DMS/CMS access groups are defined by the data classification standard is classification-driven access authorization (DCH-01.4) enforcing media access restriction (DCH-03), ISO 8.3.
Publishing DMS/CMS document metadata into the entity's Data Catalog is population of the Data Catalog (GOV-10.1).

Selecting DMS/WCMS/collaboration tooling with OCR, indexing, versioning, secured access and global search is a technology acquisition decision (TDA-01) whose search/discovery requirement is information search and retrieval (DCH-14.1).
Document volume, DMS user counts and percentage of paper migrated are program key performance indicators (GOV-05.1).
A plan to build out target data architecture capabilities is alignment with enterprise architecture (SEA-02) driven by a strategic plan and objectives artifact (PRM-01.1).

A policy requiring the target data architecture to be built alongside the enterprise architecture using a recognized EA framework (TOGAF/Zachman) with models kept current is enterprise architecture alignment (SEA-02) under documented architecture principles (SEA-01.4).

Baselining current conceptual/logical/physical data models, key processes and visualized data flows and lineage is data flow diagramming (AST-04) within enterprise architecture (SEA-02), with the lineage element matching PRI-09.

Defining the future-state enterprise data model and target architecture is the target-state side of enterprise architecture alignment (SEA-02), documented as data flow and architecture diagrams (AST-04).
A documented current-to-target architecture gap analysis feeding an initiative list is architecture alignment work (SEA-02) recorded as tracked capability deficiencies (IAO-05).

Documenting data lake requirements against a vendor-neutral big data reference architecture is an architecture and platform acquisition decision (SEA-02, TDA-01); SCF has no big-data-specific control.

A data partitioning strategy for real-time and batch processing is a performance-optimization architecture choice (SEA-02) with a capacity/performance objective (CAP-01), not the security partitioning SEA-03.1 describes.
Adopting a single diagramming notation such as UML for entity structures across the SDLC is standardized terminology and representation (SEA-02.1) supporting architecture diagramming (AST-04).
Tooling for architecture design, data modeling and data lineage capture to enable impact analysis is data flow diagramming (AST-04) plus data lineage (PRI-09).

A process to review, approve and implement changes to current and target data architectures, including modifications to Statement of Architecture Work documents, is a change management program (CHG-01) with configuration change control (CHG-02).
Mandatory architecture checkpoints in the SDLC that validate model conformance to the enterprise data model are SDLC management gates (PRM-07) implemented as design reviews (TDA-06.5).
Metrics tracking progress from current-state toward target-state data architecture are program key performance indicators (GOV-05.1).

A register holding architecture project documentation, reference materials and data model designs is the retention of technical documentation artifacts (TDA-22) against defined documentation requirements (TDA-04).

Inventorying all data sources, systems, applications and data stores and documenting high-level lineage and data models is asset inventory (AST-02) with data flow diagrams (AST-04) and lineage documentation (PRI-09).
A target data integration architecture with requirements, a conceptual diagram and a component list is enterprise architecture alignment (SEA-02) captured as architecture/data flow diagrams (AST-04).
A Data Integration Plan sequencing implementation of the target integration architecture is a strategic plan and objectives artifact (PRM-01.1) executing the architecture (SEA-02).

Training staff involved in data sharing on handling practices and on the consequences of unauthorized disclosure or mishandling is training on sensitive/regulated data storage, handling and processing (SAT-03.3) within the awareness program (SAT-02).

An Integration Requirements Document capturing scope, timeline, resources, cost and functional/non-functional requirements is requirements definition (PRM-05) at the product requirement stage (TDA-02).
A solution design document with a solution overview, data flow diagram and source-to-target mapping is developer architecture and design documentation (TDA-05) expressed as DFDs (AST-04).

Integration and functional testing with defined test cases executed in a test environment before production release is security/acceptance testing throughout development (TDA-09) requiring separated test and production environments (TDA-08), ISO 8.29.
Post-release monitoring with defect reporting and change requests for new user requirements is ongoing monitoring of the deployed solution (TDA-09.1) feeding configuration change control (CHG-02).
A documented and followed ETL extract/transform/load procedure is a data engineering pipeline; the only SCF analogue is the requirement for standardized documented operating procedures (OPS-01.1).
A documented ELT procedure for landing raw data in the data lake before transformation is likewise only reachable as a standardized documented operating procedure (OPS-01.1).

The nine-step external data sharing process (request, classification check, principles assessment, executive approval, sharing controls, signed agreement, then release) is information sharing (DCH-14) with explicit transfer authorization (DCH-14.2) and controlled transfer of sensitive data (DCH-25), ISO 5.14.
A public website channel that receives data sharing requests and routes them to the Data Office is the intake mechanism of the information sharing control (DCH-14).
An internal data sharing agreement template with the sharing controls documented in it is a documented transfer authorization (DCH-14.2) governing internal information sharing (DCH-14).

An external data sharing agreement stating purpose, parties, lawful basis, duration and liability is information sharing with third parties (PRI-07) governed by third-party contract requirements (TPM-05) over shared information (DCH-14).

Requiring executive and requestor signature before sharing and periodic steward-led review of all ongoing agreements against their contractual provisions is review of third-party arrangements (TPM-08) against contract requirements (TPM-05).
Transfer rate, latency, request volumes, accept/deny counts and evaluation duration are program key performance indicators (GOV-05.1).
A plan to build reference and master data management capability is the data governance program (GOV-10) executed through a strategic plan artifact (PRM-01.1).

Identifying master data objects, the reference data they need and the systems where they are created, read, updated and deleted is data governance (GOV-10) building on the asset/system inventory (AST-02).

Categorizing reference data as internal (entity is single source of truth) or external (owned by another entity or a standards body) is an ownership determination (AST-03) within data governance (GOV-10).
Categorizing master data objects by whether the entity owns them and is the single source of truth is data ownership assignment (AST-03) under the data governance program (GOV-10).

Documented requirements for lifecycle processes and roles, golden-record matching rules, provisioning to consuming applications and data quality requirements is data governance (GOV-10) with an explicit data quality management dependency (PRI-10).
Evaluating and selecting a master data hub architecture design is an architecture decision (SEA-02) and a technology selection (TDA-01); SCF has no MDM-specific control.
Choosing between registry, repository and coexistence hub patterns is a pure information-architecture pattern decision, reachable only through enterprise architecture alignment (SEA-02).

An information architecture listing reference/master data objects with metadata definitions, models, sources, matching rules and data flows is architecture documentation (SEA-02) with a catalog/metadata inventory (GOV-10.1) and data flow diagrams (AST-04).

Documented hub technical requirements covering workflows, version control, functional and API-integration capability and support for secure data exchange is requirements definition (PRM-05) including baseline security requirements for the product (TDA-02).
Training on identification, matching, consolidation, conflict resolution and change management for staff who manage reference and master data is role-based training (SAT-03).
Assigning Business and IT Data Stewards to every identified reference and master data object is the data stewardship control (DCH-01.1).

A process covering creation, modification and archiving of reference and master data objects is data governance lifecycle management (GOV-10) whose archiving step is archived data sets (DCH-20) under retention rules (DCH-18).

Instantiating the hub components, loading objects and activating replication/synchronization is the build-out of the designed architecture (SEA-02) under the data governance program (GOV-10); SCF has no implementation-specific control.

Establishing the hub as the entity's trusted source that new systems must consume is authoritative-source governance (GOV-10) serving data quality operations (DCH-22); SCF's nearest named analogue, PRI-04.2 primary sources, is scoped to personal data only.
SLAs balancing time against cost for reference and master data changes are performance targets (GOV-05) over the data operations process (DCH-22); SCF has no internal-SLA control.
Incorrect-value counts, MTTR for RMD quality issues and change request volumes are program key performance indicators (GOV-05.1).

A register of reference and master data change request logs and the decisions taken on them is the change record produced by configuration change control (CHG-02) under a change management program (CHG-01).

Retaining Statement of Architecture Work documents for RMD initiatives is the retention of technical documentation artifacts (TDA-22); nothing in SCF addresses architecture-work registers specifically.
A BI and analytics plan with roadmap, milestones, resources and budget is a strategic plan and objectives artifact (PRM-01.1) inside the data governance program (GOV-10).

Ideation workshops producing a long list of analytics use cases which is then shortlisted is business portfolio prioritization; only the strategic planning control (PRM-01.1) touches it, and only loosely.

Detailing each use case with objective, analytics type, ROI, stakeholders, requirements, feeding data sources and technologies is requirements definition (PRM-05); documenting which data sources feed which processing is data action mapping (AST-02.8).

An implementation plan running requirements, high-level design, staging and production environment preparation, development and testing is SDLC management (PRM-07) requiring separation of development, test and production environments (TDA-08).
Upskilling analytics staff on data preparation, model development, analytics tooling and evaluation techniques is role-based training (SAT-03).
Campaigns publicizing existing analytics assets for reuse, success stories and new tools is organizational knowledge sharing (SAT-05) building workforce capability (SAT-01).

Validating each use case against its intended purpose and against the privacy domain's personal data protection considerations is a data protection impact assessment (RSK-10) enforcing purpose limitation on processing (PRI-04).

Standing up a data analytics team of data scientists, engineers and visualization engineers is definition of roles and responsibilities (HRS-03) driven by an identification of critical skills (HRS-13).
Counts of use cases defined, piloted, implemented, total ROI and training sessions delivered are program key performance indicators (GOV-05.1).
A read-accessible register of BI use cases, outcome reviews and process documentation is retention of technical documentation artifacts (TDA-22) as program work products (CPL-13).

Identifying data revenue-generation and cost-saving use cases under the national Data Revenue Framework is commercial data monetization; SCF has no control covering productizing or selling organizational data (PRI-20 addresses data brokers as regulated third parties, not an entity monetizing its own data), so this is an honest gap.
Only the roadmap/resources/budget half of this specification is reachable, as a strategic plan and objectives artifact (PRM-01.1); the payback-period and ROI estimation half has no SCF equivalent.
Selecting and documenting a pricing scheme model for each data product is a commercial pricing decision with no security, privacy or governance control equivalent anywhere in SCF.
Calculating total cost of a data product from collection and development cost is cost accounting; SCF contains no financial costing control.
Choosing a charging model (subscription, consumption, freemium, one-time fee) is a commercial billing decision outside the entire SCF catalog.

Submitting a revenue generation request with pricing documentation to NDMO is a local regulatory filing specific to the KSA Data Revenue Framework; SCF has no analogue for pricing approval submissions.
Measuring realized ROI and payback against projections is performance measurement (GOV-05); the change-request and defect-reporting half is configuration change control (CHG-02).

Counts of data products developed, requests raised, revenue generated, cost saved, payback period and ROI are program key performance indicators (GOV-05.1), even though the underlying subject is commercial.
A plan coordinating which datasets get published openly is governance of publicly accessible content (DCH-15) delivered through a strategic plan artifact (PRM-01.1).
Campaigns making external users aware of the open data offered is outward promotion of publicly accessible content (DCH-15); SCF's nearest internal analogue is knowledge sharing (SAT-05).
Processes to identify publishable datasets, publish and maintain them at quality while ensuring the exclusion of any restricted data is exactly the publicly accessible content control (DCH-15).

Assessing whether combining the dataset with other publicly available data could disclose personal information or create a privacy risk before publishing is statistical disclosure control (DCH-23.5) and de-identification (DCH-23) applied to publicly accessible content (DCH-15).
Publishing identified datasets under the KSA Open Data License is release of publicly accessible content (DCH-15) subject to defined usage/licensing terms (DCH-27).
Documenting the metadata that lets a published open dataset be identified, described and searched is metadata/catalog management (GOV-10.1) applied to publicly accessible content (DCH-15).

Mandating machine-readable formats (CSV, JSON, XML, RDF) plus usage documentation is a publication-format standard; SCF only reaches it as a property of publicly accessible content (DCH-15) and has no format-interoperability control.

Regularly updating published datasets, reviewing them against regulatory requirements and maintaining traceability through documented provenance and version history is maintenance of publicly accessible content (DCH-15) with provenance (AST-03.2) and data quality operations (DCH-22).
Downloads per dataset, datasets identified, published and updated are program key performance indicators (GOV-05.1).

A register of all identified open datasets with a log of activities and decisions taken is the recordkeeping side of publicly accessible content management (DCH-15), retained as program work products (CPL-13).
A plan to achieve and maintain compliance with the NDMO Freedom of Information Regulations is the identification of and planning against applicable statutory obligations (CPL-01).
Campaigns raising staff awareness of FOI obligations and citizens' access rights are awareness training (SAT-02) with role-targeted content for those processing FOI requests (SAT-03).

Designing a standardized request-for-information process per the FOI Regulations is operationalizing a statutory obligation (CPL-01) governing release of public information (DCH-15); SCF's PRI-06 data subject rights is deliberately not used because FOI is a public-transparency right, not a data subject right.
Deciding within a statutory deadline to grant, deny, extend or redirect an access request is a controlled disclosure of information decision (DCH-03.1) discharging a statutory obligation (CPL-01).
Proactively publishing laws, services, organizational structure, vacancies, reports and statistics on the official website is the publicly accessible content control (DCH-15).

Prescribing the content of the access request form (requestor identity, national ID, description, purpose, legal basis, delivery method) is a regulator-specified form design; only the statutory compliance control (CPL-01) covers it, and only as an obligation to meet.
Calculating a processing fee for each granted access request using an NDMO pricing scheme is fee determination; SCF contains no pricing or cost-recovery control, so this is a genuine gap.

Internal audits of FOI compliance with findings reported to the ODIA and corrective actions plus regulator notification on non-compliance is the internal audit function (CPL-02.1), periodic audits (CPL-02.2) and corrective action (CPL-02.3).

A register holding FOI compliance records, access request records and publication records is retention of compliance work products (CPL-13), the request-record element being an accounting of disclosures (PRI-14.1).
A plan with roadmap, milestones, resources and budget to classify the entity's data is the data and asset classification control (DCH-02, ISO 5.12) carried by a strategic plan artifact (PRM-01.1).
Producing a ranked list of datasets and artifacts to determine classification order is the scoping step of data and asset classification (DCH-02).

Assigning handling and protection controls to datasets by classification level so handling, processing, sharing and disposal are secure is protection of sensitive/regulated data driven by classification (DCH-01.2) under the data protection control (DCH-01).

Identifying and inventorying all datasets and artifacts the entity owns, using the Data Catalog where implemented, is a sensitive data inventory (DCH-06.2) and asset inventory (AST-02) held in the catalog (GOV-10.1), i.e. ISO 5.9.

Assessing the impact of unauthorized access across national interest, organizations, individuals and environment and deriving Top Secret / Secret / Confidential / Public levels is impact-based security categorization (RSK-02) producing the classification (DCH-02, ISO 5.12).

Evaluating whether 'Low' impact data can be released as Public instead of Confidential, weighing regulatory breach against benefit of opening it, is a deliberate downward reclassification (DCH-11) of previously assigned levels (DCH-02).
Reviewing all classified datasets to confirm the assigned level is still the most appropriate is the periodic reclassification review (DCH-11) of the classification scheme (DCH-02, ISO 5.12).

Publishing the assigned classification level as metadata against each dataset in the catalog is marking/labelling (DCH-04, ISO 5.13) implemented as data protection attributes (DCH-05) held in the Data Catalog (GOV-10.1).
Percentages of datasets classified, classified by level, low-impact treated as confidential and reviewed/approved are program key performance indicators (GOV-05.1).

A register listing every dataset with its assigned classification level, assignment dates, classification duration and review outcomes is a sensitive data inventory (DCH-06.2, ISO 5.9) recording classification decisions (DCH-02) in the catalog (GOV-10.1).

Identifying the types of personal data collected, where and how it is stored, its current processing and uses, and the gaps to regulatory compliance is a personal data inventory (PRI-05.5) with documented processing activities (PRI-14) and an initial privacy impact assessment (RSK-10), ISO 5.34.

A Personal Data Protection Plan addressing strategic and operational privacy requirements with roadmap, resources and budget is the data privacy program (PRI-01) instantiated through a strategic plan artifact (PRM-01.1).

Training every employee on personal data definitions, data subject rights, entity responsibilities and notification handling is the training element of personal data control testing, training and monitoring (PRI-08) delivered as role-based training (SAT-03).

Notifying the Regulatory Authority within 72 hours of determining personal data was compromised is cyber incident reporting for sensitive/regulated data (IRO-10.2) under the data breach plan (IRO-04.1) through regulator contacts (IRO-14).

Documented breach management procedures with roles, incident review with the regulator, immediate response, permanent corrective actions and testing of those actions is the data breach plan (IRO-04.1) executed through incident handling (IRO-02) and root cause analysis / lessons learned (IRO-13).

Providing notice and obtaining implicit or explicit consent at every collection point, publishing a reviewable privacy notice and maintaining a hyperlink to it online is the privacy notice control (PRI-02), data subject consent (PRI-03) and the conspicuous link requirement (PRI-17.1), ISO 5.34.

Supporting the rights to be informed, access, rectification, erasure, objection, restriction and portability with a submission and tracking mechanism is data subject empowerment (PRI-06) including right to erasure (PRI-06.5) and data portability (PRI-06.6).

Yearly risk assessments of every system collecting, processing, storing or transmitting personal data, with findings documented, analyzed for impact and likelihood and evaluated against regulatory obligations, is a data protection impact assessment (RSK-10) run as a formal risk assessment (RSK-04).

Internal audits of privacy compliance reported to the DPO with corrective actions and regulator notification on non-compliance is the internal audit function (CPL-02.1) running periodic audits (CPL-02.2) over privacy controls (PRI-08).

A register retaining for at least 24 months a record of any collection or processing of personal data, producible on regulator request, is documentation of data processing activities (PRI-14) backed by the personal data inventory (PRI-05.5).

Establishing a plan of tools, personnel and business processes so security meets the entity's data protection needs is the security program control (GOV-01) with assigned responsibilities (GOV-04), matching ISO 5.1 policies and 5.2 roles.

Fundamental system concepts and properties that provide the context and guidance for security design decisions is secure engineering principles (SEA-01) aligned to enterprise architecture (SEA-02), i.e. ISO 8.27 secure system architecture and engineering principles.

Minimum security provisions built into a system during development, testing and implementation is secure software development practices (TDA-06) with security testing throughout development (TDA-09), ISO 8.25 and 8.29.

Establishing the identity of users and systems requesting access to information assets is the identity and access management program (IAC-01) with provisioning/de-provisioning (IAC-07) and access enforcement (IAC-20), covering ISO 5.15/5.16/5.18.
Reflecting information security requirements in third-party supplier engagements is third-party management (TPM-01) with contractual security requirements (TPM-05), ISO 5.19 and 5.20.
A comprehensive information security training program introducing personnel to security expectations and obligations is awareness training (SAT-02) plus role-based training (SAT-03), ISO 6.3.
A documented and maintained inventory of information assets containing critical entity data is asset governance (AST-01) and asset inventories (AST-02), ISO 5.9.

Operational duties to monitor, assess and protect information assets is operations security (OPS-01) delivered through continuous monitoring (MON-01), ISO 8.16 monitoring activities and 5.37 documented operating procedures.

Processes for detecting, managing, recording and analyzing security threats and breaches arising from monitoring is incident response operations (IRO-01) governed by an incident response plan (IRO-04), ISO 5.24 and 5.26.

Identification, review, response and corrective action for risks by likelihood, consequence and exposure is the risk management program (RSK-01) with risk assessment (RSK-04) and risk remediation (RSK-06); ISO 27002:2022 has no risk-management clause of its own (it sits in ISO 27001 clause 6), so iso_clauses is deliberately empty.

A framework preserving confidentiality, integrity and availability of data during an incident is the business continuity management system (BCD-01) with BC/DR plans (BCD-01.7), ISO 5.29 security during disruption and 5.30 ICT readiness for business continuity.
